title: bug: the lander durably refuses on a TRANSIENT verified-workspace capture failure and never retries
description:
Found by worker-883dc9b4 during the adversarial review of task-29f367530d954a18a8580f184b09c65d (parent row). node-lander.ts records EVERY checkLandingVerification failure through refuse(), a durable landing receipt, and landOne then returns null for that acceptance forever. But capture can fail transiently: git-verified-workspace-capture.ts:63 raises VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_DRIFT when HEAD moves mid-capture, and a 30s git timeout surfaces as VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED. The lander's own observe path already follows the opposite house rule, at the "reported, not recorded: the next pass retries" comment in landOne, so a one-off git hiccup permanently burns an ACCEPTED delivery, with no retry and no credit.

This PRE-DATES the parent row on the delivered path, where it is worse because real work is lost. The parent's hoist extends the same exposure to genuine no-ops, which previously answered NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and were credited by landedWithNoEffect. Fix sketch: classify capture refusal codes into structural and transient, and return transient ones unrecorded, the way the observe path does. dependsOn the parent because both rows edit landOne in node-lander.ts.

implementationPlan.description:
WRITE THE FAILING ARM FIRST: a transient capture failure must not burn the delivery. DoD item 2.

Drive VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_DRIFT, which is the cleanest transient case - capture raises it when HEAD or the branch ref moves between the first and final read. Assert that NO durable landing receipt was written, by reading the landing ledger back, not by inspecting the returned report. Then assert a later pass, with capture succeeding, DOES land.

Today the first pass writes a receipt and landOne returns null for that acceptance forever, so this arm must go red. Quote the red.

Assert the specific code on the report, and the absence of the receipt. An arm that only asserts 'it did not land' would pass for the wrong reason.

implementationPlan.description:
THE CLOSED CLASSIFICATION MAP. DoD item 1, and the part most likely to be done loosely.

Add a total map from refusal code to transient-or-structural over the roster you enumerated in step 1. NO DEFAULT ARM: defaulting to transient livelocks on a new structural code, defaulting to structural burns real deliveries on a new transient one. A code that is not in the map must fail the build or fail a test, not inherit a guess.

Structural, and these must stay durably recorded: LANDING_VERIFIER_BINDING_MISSING, LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_UNCONFIGURED, LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED, and the capture codes that describe repository configuration rather than a moment in time - submodule, filter and ref-backend unsupported. Transient: DRIFT and the shared invoker's GIT_FAILED. Decide VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_UNKNOWN deliberately and say why in the step note; it is the genuinely ambiguous one and either choice needs a reason.

Then change the one line in landOne: refuse durably for structural, return the bare report for transient, exactly as the observe path twenty lines above already does. Keep the house-rule comment adjacent so the two paths read as one rule.
implementationPlan.note:
CLOSED MAP in node-lander-verification.ts (83 lines): LANDING_VERIFICATION_REFUSALS, frozen, covering exactly the 10 reachable codes from step 1. There is NO default:
- landingVerificationClass(code) returns the class via Object.hasOwn, or null for any code not in the table (including prototype keys).
- unrecordedLandingReport(refusal, nodeRef) gives TRANSIENT codes {detail, nodeRef, outcome: <code>}, the same shape as the observe path; returns null for STRUCTURAL, so the caller records it; and gives any other code a distinct stable outcome LANDING_VERIFICATION_UNCLASSIFIED with detail "<code>: <detail>".
- So an unlisted code inherits NEITHER class: it is not recorded, and the runtime does not retry it (the coordinator contains it in BLOCKED). The roster arm proves the production port cannot reach that branch.

CLASSES:
- STRUCTURAL: BINDING_MISSING, UNCONFIGURED, CHANGED, SUBMODULE/FILTER/REF_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED. The verifier's own capture succeeded on this workspace, which is a precondition of acceptance, so any of the last three means configuration changed after verification.
- TRANSIENT: DRIFT, GIT_FAILED, plus two decided here:
  - UNKNOWN -> TRANSIENT. It is the refuser's fallback for any non-VerifiedGitFailure throw. In practice that means a path that vanished or was locked between `git status` and lstat/read (ENOENT, or Windows EBUSY/EPERM, including the scratch rmSync in withVerifiedGit's finally). Its parse guards on git's -z output never fire in practice. Recording it destroys an ACCEPTED delivery irreversibly over an unknown cause, while retrying is visible each pass and heals itself.
  - IDENTITY_UNKNOWN (not named by the plan) -> TRANSIENT. The identity git calls fail (10s rev-parse timeout, a spawn failure, rev-parse HEAD exiting neither 0 nor 1) moments after observe found a repository in the same pass. A workspace that is really gone gets observe's durable NOT_A_REPOSITORY on the next pass, so the one structural cause cannot livelock.

LANDONE (node-lander.ts :217-222): `return unrecordedLandingReport(checked, nodeRef) ?? refuse(...)`, with the house-rule comment next to it. The header doc now says structural refusals are recorded and moments are retried. The file is 283 lines (277 before, 250 target, 400 split).

SCOPE +1 production file: repository-delivery-runtime.ts land() now returns RETRY for GIT_INDEX_LOCKED OR landingVerificationClass(outcome)==="TRANSIENT", using the same table. The RED proves it is needed. The new runtime arm "re-queues a transient capture failure and lands the same acceptance once the moment passes" uses a real repo and the real port: verify with landing off, `git checkout --detach`, advance. With ONLY the lander fix it gave EXIT=1: `- "phase": "AWAITING_LANDING"` / `+ "phase": "BLOCKED"`, the permanent wedge, with log `[lander] a: VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED (VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED)`. With the runtime line the arm is green: no receipt, landing aggregate version unchanged, reservation AWAITING_LANDING; after `git checkout main`, advance lands keep.txt and the reservation is released.

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW DONE, re-derived this session against the delivered bytes rather than inherited. Full record in comment-5f7bbe84c9554c85b70a257d599e2253; the prior seat's pass is comment-31c540ab (read and re-verified, not trusted blind).

NEW FINDING, CLEARED: the runtime classifies `report.outcome` through the same table, and VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED (TRANSIENT) is ALSO raised POST-INTENT by git-verified-workspace-commit.ts:39,64. A raw code there would make the runtime retry a landing that may already have moved HEAD. It cannot happen: node-lander.ts:243 routes every non-recovery, non-INDEX_LOCKED commit failure through refuse(), which reports outcome "REFUSED" (:166), never the raw code. refuse()'s only fallback outcome is the ledger's own failure code, and landing-ledger.ts:29-37 enumerates those as EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT / LANDING_RECEIPT_INVALID / LANDING_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND / LANDING_BASELINE_INVALID — none a table key. The retry branch is reachable only from the pre-intent verification check.

DoD ITEM 5, ANSWERED EXPLICITLY: retry is UNBOUNDED. No counter, no deadline, deliberately identical to the observe path twenty lines above, which this row exists to make the second path obey. It is not silent — repository-delivery-runtime.ts:119 logs `[lander] <nodeRef>: <outcome> (<detail>)` on every pass, so a workspace whose HEAD moves each cycle prints VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_DRIFT every pass. What it deliberately lacks is a DURABLE receipt, because a receipt consumes the acceptance forever. A bound is a separate design decision and belongs in its own row; the raw observe path carries the same unbounded shape today and is already spun out as task-65a594816ed5460f999fbd46f40c5cea.

VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_UNKNOWN -> TRANSIENT, and why. It is the refuser's fallback for any non-VerifiedGitFailure throw — in practice a path that vanished or was locked between `git status` and the read of its bytes. STRUCTURAL there would destroy an ACCEPTED delivery irreversibly over a cause nobody has identified; TRANSIENT heals itself on the next pass, and a workspace that is genuinely gone is still caught durably by the observe path's NOT_A_REPOSITORY.
